notes: All observations use real SplitEdge component picks, one-shot feature clicks and actual Undo/Redo in owned private Xvfb sessions. Only public Rhino commands/APIs were used.
Portable requests substitute the exact source recipe for the existing shared box artifact. Response values are compacted as JSON but not numerically normalized or reordered within arrays.

Eleven declared Mid/End targets match complete native geometry/attribute/history replay at absolute 1e-9 and relative 1e-10. Native feature enumeration is independently checked against those targets. Neither check proves screen hit-test equivalence.

The first mixed-polycurve Cen click did not capture the intended center. The model-target adapter predicts x=4, while Rhino's recorded unsnapped position is x=2.776693248934896. This is an explicit retained discrepancy, not a twelfth passing replay.

Five additional Center diagnostics compare standalone and composite arcs. Clicks at the empty center miss; clicks near the arc capture its center in both representations. This establishes hover dependence for these cases, not a general rejection of polycurve arc centers.
Center diagnostics lack recorded camera calibration. They are not counted as native pixel replays or used to substitute Rhino output positions into the input fixtures.

Native standalone Center capture remains point-based; composite Center capture is not implemented. Hover-aware curve discovery, one-shot mode semantics, occlusion and arbitrary rational-curve recognition remain incomplete.

The retained raw outputs contain complete source/target geometry and unchanged external targets through command and history replay. Earlier snap, distance and unconstrained SplitEdge archives remain unchanged.
